short: Proclaimed at York, he fought through eighteen years of civil war to reunite and refound the empire.
full:
Constantine was proclaimed emperor by his father's troops at Eboracum, modern York, on 25 July 306 CE, one claimant among several under the tetrarchic system Diocletian had designed to prevent exactly this kind of dispute. He spent the following eighteen years defeating rival emperors in turn, eliminating his last competitor, Licinius, in 324 CE to become sole ruler of a reunified empire.

Constantine reorganised the army and currency, introducing the solidus gold coin that would remain stable for centuries, and in 330 CE dedicated a new capital at Byzantium, refounded as Constantinople, shifting the empire's centre of gravity permanently eastward. He died on 22 May 337 CE, dividing the empire among his three surviving sons, and is remembered as the emperor who ended the third-century pattern of rapid civil war and restored a single, lasting imperial house.
